mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a single month signals supply chain disruptions, which increases costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS declines simultaneously
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decline in housing starts (HOUST) during a period of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, particularly during periods of high inflation.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines while CPIAUCSL is rising
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the interaction effect of HOUST declines and CPIAUCSL rises on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during high inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of INDPRO declines and CPIAUCSL rises on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during stagflation periods.
